implementation_state: All three of this node's gates are met and were measured rather than inherited: the account contract and its pure calculations are five test targets and 47 tests, persistence and runtime ownership are AppState holding an AccountStore behind the optional feature with a store-keying fixture that runs in the default build, and default-build compatibility is a property of the feature tables — zroutery-core is declared by the desktop package with no features at all, and account, newapi and account-maint are declared there and now all three are in the desktop's default list, so the shipped app carries them. ML feature order is untouched: `ml` is still first in that list and the core's own feature table is unchanged, so the learning build is not perturbed. The exclusion these clauses recorded was written against a sentence that has since expired — "nothing probes an account, so with this on the store is constructed and stays empty" — and the reconciler that made it untrue is why the default list can carry them now. Execution, the missing third of that boundary, now exists too as AppState::reconcile_accounts, with the maintenance declaration's scheduler and the observation layer's consumer on top of it. The previous text said persistence and production ownership/execution were absent, which has been untrue since before E-119 corrected the identical sentence on ACCOUNT; this row is the second time that clause was found false, and the fix was to measure the gates rather than to correct the prose again. THIS NODE IS SUPERSEDED BY ACCOUNT AND SAYING DONE DOES NOT MEAN THE ACCOUNT WORK IS DONE: Stage 5's gates were about existence, not integration, and what is still unexercised and still unwired is recorded on ACCOUNT and UI-NEW-TRACKS rather than folded into this row. See E-133.

notes: Account remains optional and is not enabled by the default Tauri dependency.

Revalidated rather than advanced. DONE here is a claim about this node's three gates and nothing wider: a reader who takes this row as 'accounts work' would be wrong, because the account node's remaining surface and integration gaps are recorded on ACCOUNT and UI-NEW-TRACKS, not here.

THE SHIPPED APP NOW CARRIES THE CAPABILITIES ITS OWN INTERFACE OFFERS. The desktop's default feature list was `["ml"]`, so the account subsystem, the NewAPI panel adapter, the browser check-in and the OpenCode provider kinds were all absent from the installed app — while the dashboard offered the account page, the check-in and both OpenCode kinds unconditionally. The panel said "this build contains no account subsystem" to the very people the product was written for, and the panel-backed balance was in the source tree and in no installation of it. **THE REASON THESE WERE KEPT OUT HAS EXPIRED, AND THE REASON IS WORTH KEEPING.** It was "the surface is not reachable yet: nothing probes an account, so with this on the store is constructed and stays empty". The reconciler landed, every declared account is probed and published, and that sentence no longer describes the code. **"OPTIONAL" NOW MEANS WHAT IT SHOULD MEAN: THE CAPABILITY IS IN THE BINARY AND THE BEHAVIOUR IS NOT.** Nothing probes an account until an account is declared; nothing asks a panel until an account exists and the button is pressed; no browser opens until the operator starts a check-in; the OpenCode providers only answer when one is configured. That is the shape ADR-0006 settled on for the learning stack, where `ml_routing.enabled` still defaults to off and an installation that has never promoted a model routes exactly as it did before. `--no-default-features` still builds a desktop app with none of it, so "ship without an account subsystem" remains a build rather than a deletion. The desktop's dependency line on `zroutery-core` still names no features at all, so the core's switches stay independently declared and the activation guard is untouched; `ml` is still first in the default list; and the core's own feature table is unchanged, so the learning build is not perturbed. See E-158.

THE CLAUSE "ACCOUNT REMAINS OPTIONAL AND IS NOT ENABLED BY THE DEFAULT TAURI DEPENDENCY" WAS TRUE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN AND IS NOT TRUE NOW, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT. It was written while the account surface was unreachable — the note this record repeats, that nothing probes an account, so with the feature on the store is constructed and stays empty. The reconciler landed and that sentence stopped describing the code. The desktop's default feature list now carries `account`, `newapi` and `account-maint`, so the shipped app holds the capability, and the capability is inert until the operator declares an account and presses a button — which is what "optional" should have meant all along, and is what ADR-0006 settled on for the learning stack. The plan document `account-surface-plan.md` carries the constraint as a load-bearing one, so it carries a dated note saying that it has been superseded and why; the plan itself is left as it was written, because a plan that is rewritten after the fact is not a record. `--no-default-features` still builds the app without any of it. See E-158.
